transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-03-20 09:30 PT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee, Priya Kapoor, Ethan Morris (Redwood); Carlos Ramirez, Maya Chen, Lena Novak, Omar Ahmed (MediScale)
Link: benchmark spreadsheet (shared) - tinyurl.com/mediscale-bench (note: link shortened in chat)

Summary (auto): quick review of this week's runs. Some improvement on median latency vs baseline but tail still elevated for a small subset.

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone thanks for joining, we'll kick off, Priya is going to run us through this week's numbers. we had a couple of new runs against the 8k context set and also a longer prompt test, ok priya over to you
[00:22] Priya: yep thanks jordan, hi all - i'll share my screen, um so slide one is the p50 p95 p99 table from yesterday's runs, redwood is blue, baseline provider is orange, p50 we're seeing about 80ms vs 110ms, p95 220ms vs 260ms, p99 480ms vs 430ms — so median and p95 are improved, p99 is slightly worse in our config, which is interesting
[00:50] Carlos: hang on p99 worse? i thought you said overall better, what's going on with the tail
[00:58] Priya: yeah it's a small subset — we believe it's network variance + cold kv cache misses. we ran with a smaller kv prewarm than baseline, and a few samples hit the cold path which bumps the p99. also note that some of the baseline runs were on a slightly different prompt length distribution so that skews it
[01:17] Maya: can you remind me what infra you used for the redwood runs? gpu type, and quantization?
[01:24] Priya: sure — dedicated G5-like instances, int8 quantization for the main model, but we toggled int4 for one run. most of today's runs used continuous batching with 50ms max latency slack and a kv cache prewarm to 75% of the working set
[01:43] Lena: and your baseline provider — what were they running, ProviderX?
[01:47] Priya: the baseline is their on-prem cluster, older A100 nodes, no quantization, single-threaded runtime; they had a larger prewarm but less efficient batching. so it's a mixed bag
[02:00] Ethan: one thing to note — our runtime prioritizes throughput vs tail at the scheduler level, so you can tune for stricter tail bounds by lowering batch windows and increasing reserved slots, but that will raise cost per token
[02:18] Omar: cost is going to be a big factor — right now their per-token math looks better on-prem but our ops team thinks we can get comparable unit cost with batching and caching optimizations
[02:30] Jordan: yeah, which is why we included a cost/latency tradeoff slide — but first, priya can you walk thru the throughput/concurrency chart
[02:37] Priya: sure - so at 150 QPS sustained our redwood config hits 120 tokens/s per GPU and an aggregate throughput of ~18k tokens/s across 6 GPUs; baseline was 14k tokens/s with higher variance under bursts. when we pushed concurrency up to 300 QPS we saw queueing increase; redwood maintained lower median latency but tail widened at 300 QPS
[03:05] Maya: what's your packet size — like average prompt+response tokens? we usually do 120 prompt, 180 gen so about 300 tokens total
[03:12] Priya: yeah that matches our long test for today (we also ran a 1.2x prompt length test to simulate your longer docs)
[03:20] [04:00] Jordan: interruption — quick check, did we do TCP keepalive/VPC peering for the test or public egress?
[04:07] Priya: these runs were over VPC peering with optimized MTU, but we had a fallback run over internet egress — the internet runs had ~15-25ms extra variance which contributed to the tail
[04:23] Lena: so some of that p99 could be network then, not the model or runtime?
[04:27] Priya: yep, exactly, it's a combination — network jitter + occasional cold kv misses + concurrency spikes
[04:35] Carlos: how reproducible are the p99 spikes? can you show timestamps or specific request ids?
[04:41] Priya: we annotated the spreadsheet with trace ids for the top 40 p99 samples, i'll upload full traces after the call. but broadly they're concentrated in a 2-3 minute window during the heavier burst test
[04:55] Maya: could those be GC pauses in your runtime?
[04:58] Ethan: unlikely, our runtime uses minimal GC for the hot path, most pauses are either kernel scheduling or kv cache loads; we did see one outlier that lines up with a background checkpoint job in the client's cluster — so local infra can show up in the traces
[05:16] Omar: interesting. on cost, if we tighten batching to reduce tail, how much does cost go up?
[05:22] Priya: rough estimate — if you cut batch window from 50ms to 20ms and reserve slots for high-priority traffic, cost per token increases by about 12-18% depending on QPS. tradeoff is more predictable latency
[05:34] Jordan: and we can include a canary — route 10% traffic to a tail-optimized policy and measure user-facing impact before rolling
[05:40] Maya: that would be helpful. also we need to validate with our end-to-end SLA tests (front-end + model) not just raw model latency
[05:48] Priya: absolutely. we recommend running the E2E scripts in the repo; maya if you can share your front-end harness we'll plug it into our runner
[05:55] Maya: i'll do that, sending the harness link after this call
[06:00] Jordan: ok next topic — quantization differences. you saw the int4 run, what did that do to throughput/quality
[06:07] Priya: int4 gave ~1.4x throughput boost but we saw small drop in long-tail coherence in one prompt category; for your use case (short form summarization) int4 looks acceptable, but for instruction-heavy prompts we prefer int8 for parity
[06:22] Carlos: quality is critical — even a subtle regression in answer style can be a blocker
[06:27] Ethan: we can lock a validation prompt set and run a side-by-side call with win-rate metrics. Redwood's eval harness can produce win/loss and ngram diffs, we'll include that in the sheet
[06:40] Maya: ok do that, and include the prompt seeds we've been using
[06:44] Priya: noted
[06:46] [08:00] Jordan: new item — network topology. lena you mentioned earlier some concerns around VPC peering, do we need a private deployment or will VPC peering suffice?
[08:09] Lena: for now peering is ok but we need to validate KMS key policies and ensure egress is locked down. if latency/p99 doesn't meet our SLA we may ask for Private deployment testing in our lab
[08:23] Jordan: understood — we can provide a Private trial package and our security pack (SOC2 + audit logs + KMS options) for you to review
[08:33] Omar: can you send the security docs to legal? they asked for SAML/SSO and audit log retention details
[08:39] Jordan: yes i'll attach our security pack in the follow-up email, and include contact for compliance
[08:47] Maya: about the benchmarking harness — are you using the same random seeds and request order as our baseline? that can affect p99 comparisons
[08:55] Priya: good point — we attempted to replay their request traces but the order differs; for the next runs we'll align seed/order and include run ids for exact reproducibility
[09:05] Carlos: what's the plan to show cost parity? your slides showed projected unit cost close but we need monthly run-rate estimates at our 10M tokens/month volume
[09:15] Jordan: we'll model three scenarios in the pricing sheet: hosted (pay-as-you-go), dedicated reserved (committed capacity with lower unit cost), and dedicated + burst. i'll send scenario numbers; the punchline should be break-even by month 3 for committed workloads
[09:29] Priya: also, caching can shave 20-40% of tokens for query-heavy workflows, which materially changes the math; we've included example cache hit assumptions in the sheet
[09:40] Maya: can caching be done client-side or do you have a managed prefix cache?
[09:44] Ethan: we support both — client side TTL and Redwood-managed KV prefix cache with optional persistence. for your workload we saw ~32% reuse in today's run
[09:52] [10:00] Jordan: ok quick recap and decisions — 1) Priya to add p95/p99 traces and rsync run ids, 2) Maya to run extra tail-latency tests against your on-prem baseline and share harness, 3) Jordan to send pricing and security docs. anything else?
[10:15] Maya: one ask — include the 99.9th percentile if possible, even if noisy
[10:20] Priya: will do 99/99.9 in the next spreadsheet update
[10:24] Carlos: also can you provide an example rollout plan for canary traffic and automatic fallback to baseline provider if tail exceeds threshold
[10:32] Ethan: yes we have a playbook and config snippet, i'll put it in the repo and link it
[10:36] Omar: timeline wise we're aiming to decide on vendor by end of month, so these runs + security review are critical
[10:42] Jordan: understood — we'll prioritize. thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the sheet and schedule the SRE deep-dive for next week
[10:50] Meeting ended

Notes on transcription quality: some overlapped speech and a couple of product names transcribed incorrectly (e.g., kv cache sometimes appears as 'k-v cash' and ProviderX as 'provider ex').

References shared: benchmark spreadsheet: tinyurl.com/mediscale-bench, security pack: tinyurl.com/redwood-security-pack, rollout-playbook repo: github.com/redwood/rollout-playbooks (link shared in chat)

End of transcript.
